source: docs/orchestration.md Part B — that document is the explanation; this file is the source of truth.
note: Transcribed from B1 (the graph), B2 (the node table) and B3 (the conflict register). Every `paths` entry was verified with grep against the working tree rather than copied from the prose, which is how K11 and K12 surfaced. See mutexNotes.

phases.name: serial, alone
phases.note: Each touches everything; none may overlap. G10 -> G9 -> G8.

phases.name: decision node
phases.note: No code. Gates every future HTTP route.

phases.name: three lanes
phases.note: Separate worktrees. Merge order C -> A -> B, set by the register, not by finish time.

mutexNotes.qa/contract.md: K1 — the shared mutable artifact of this phase (A4). G1 moves seven rows; G4 and G11 each flip a deliberately-pinned assertion; G2's own acceptance test says it updates C15's MCP row. Lane B is serial internally for this reason, and K10 records that G2 collides with it from Lane A.
mutexNotes.row:C23: K1, sharpened — G1 and G4 collide on the same ROW, not merely the same file. G4 rewrites C23's NaN assertion; G1 is one of the seven rows C23 belongs to.
mutexNotes.packages/http/src/routes.ts: K9 + K11 — three nodes edit this file: G6 at the render-cap 503 (:80), G14 at renderStored's slot ordering (:183), and G11 adding the depth guard to postRender (:101). K9 caught G6/G14 and moved G14 into Lane A. It did not catch G11, which sits in Lane B.
mutexNotes.packages/mcp/src/tools.ts: K12 — G2 adds the render cap around :411; G11 adds the depth guard to resume_create. Different lanes, same file.
mutexNotes.packages/http/src/renderLimit.ts: K9 — G2 reuses it from a shared location, G14 reorders against it.
mutexNotes.fixtures/golden/: K5 — G15's template4 comment removal rewrites 3 of 25 snapshots. Phase 3, serial, re-baselined at the end with the diff explained.
mutexNotes.**: K2 — G9's repo-wide format run rewrites every file. Alone, or never. Any concurrent diff becomes unreviewable.
mutexNotes.packages/cli/src/index.ts: K13 — three nodes rewrite different regions of this file: G5 the timeout literal (lane A), G4 the --timeout parse (lane B), G1 the top-level catch (lane B). B3 never listed it. Note the separate hazard it leaves behind: G1 changes an interface the README documents, but README.md is G12's scope in lane C, and the stated merge order C -> A -> B lands G12 FIRST. Whoever closes G1 must re-check the README after, or G12 documents exit 1 and G1 immediately makes it stale.

nodes.title: Decide where the Tectonic bundle is hosted

acceptance.statement: A written decision naming the host and the checksum strategy.

nodes.why: Choosing where to host a TeX bundle has no obvious right answer and real consequences. Split from G10-b so an Opus session does not spend its reasoning on curl flags.

nodes.title: Pin the bundle, pass --bundle, split the cache key off the template hash

acceptance.statement: CI green twice consecutively with a cold cache.

nodes.why: CI's green currently depends on relay.fullyjustified.net being unthrottled, and the failure looks like a code failure. Until this lands, no downstream merge decision is trustworthy.

nodes.title: Prettier config + repo-wide run + lint script

acceptance.statement: npx prettier --check . clean; npm test unchanged at 584.

nodes.why: K2 — rewrites every file. Land it before lanes open, or defer it to the end entirely.

nodes.title: tsconfig.test.json x 5, run the typecheck, report what surfaces

acceptance.statement: The 5 configs exist; npm run build && npm test unaffected; qa/findings.md carries the real typecheck output.

nodes.why: Split from G8-b so the judgment half has real evidence instead of speculation, and so an Opus session isn't spent adding boilerplate tsconfig files. Does not wire typecheck:test into build/test yet — that is G8-c, once the errors it surfaces are triaged.

nodes.title: Triage the typecheck report, decide what is in scope to fix

acceptance.statement: Every error in G8-a's report triaged: fix now, suppress with a stated reason, or deferred as a new finding.

nodes.why: gate.md's brief says 'do not touch packages/', which is right for a pure judgment call but wrong here without G8-a's report first — this is the '(gate after the report)' node B2 describes.

nodes.title: Fix the in-scope errors, wire typecheck:test into build/test

acceptance.statement: Typecheck passes over test/; every error triaged, not silenced.

nodes.why: Implements G8-b's decision. K4 — lanes open only after the typecheck is clean, and this is the node that makes it clean.

nodes.title: Decide: is HTTP a deliberate subset or an incomplete adapter?

acceptance.statement: A decision record in docs/; qa/contract.md's two 'no surface' cells resolve to a plan.

nodes.why: K7 — gates every new HTTP route, including the citation surface. No route work in any lane until this is written down.

nodes.title: One shared default and one shared ceiling for render timeouts

acceptance.statement: Four packages read one constant; C23's bounds still hold.

nodes.why: Opus despite being a constants change — it crosses four packages, which trips the three-package clause. packages/store's LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS is a DIFFERENT concept and must not be folded in.
nodes.warn: B3 filed G5 as conflicting only with G2 (K3). It also holds routes.ts and the CLI entry point, so while G5 is open, G4, G6, G11, G14 and G1 are all withheld. Phase 2's three-lane parallelism does not survive this node — run G5 first, alone, and the lanes open behind it.

nodes.title: Render concurrency cap for MCP

acceptance.statement: Queue-vs-reject decided and written; C15's MCP row updated.

nodes.why: findings.md argues MCP should probably QUEUE rather than reject, unlike HTTP — an agent should not settle that alone. K3: G5 settles where shared adapter constants live and G2 consumes the answer; never concurrent.

nodes.title: Split render-cap 503 from lock-timeout 503

acceptance.statement: The two are distinguishable without reading the message string.

nodes.why: Sonnet despite 'medium' severity — severity measures impact, not difficulty, and C15's contract row already defines done.

nodes.title: Acquire the render slot before reading the store

acceptance.statement: C9's 'unknown id returns 404' still passes — the ordering is load-bearing.

nodes.why: K6 — a missing id must still 404, not 503. K9 moved this out of Lane C into Lane A, serial after G6.

nodes.title: Route --timeout through parseNumberFlag

acceptance.statement: C23's NaN assertion goes RED, then is rewritten to expect a usage error.

nodes.why: K8 — turning a deliberately-pinned assertion red is expected and correct. The commit must update qa/contract.md in the same change.

nodes.title: Apply the depth guard to POST /render and resume_create

acceptance.statement: C8's 'G11 still ungated' assertion goes RED, then is rewritten.

nodes.why: K8, as G4. Its two code paths are postRender (routes.ts:101) and resume_create (tools.ts) — which is why it carries the K11 and K12 mutexes that B3 missed.

nodes.title: Exit-code taxonomy: 2 usage / 3 validation / 4 render / 5 busy

acceptance.statement: Seven contract rows updated together; the change is called breaking in the commit.

nodes.why: Opus and gated because exit codes are an interface. Anything already branching on exit 1 breaks.

nodes.title: hasBinary gate for tectonic

acceptance.statement: A machine without Tectonic reports it once, not as N render failures.

nodes.why: Reuse the existing hasBinary in packages/core/test/ats.test.ts; qa/lib/env.mjs is the model. CI must keep treating a missing poppler as a hard failure, not flatten it to a skip.

nodes.title: README flag list + HTTP response-contract section
nodes.why: Genuinely disjoint. The cheapest node on which to rehearse the loop end to end.

nodes.title: Report the swallowed error in store.list()

acceptance.statement: A corrupt blueprint is visible to the caller; stderr only.

nodes.why: A similarly small change to G4 with NO test pinning it — silent failure — which pulls it toward more care despite its size (A7).

nodes.title: Three F12 residue items

acceptance.statement: Golden re-baselined WITH the diff explained.

nodes.why: K5 — rewrites 3 of 25 golden snapshots. Serial tail. Requires GOLDEN_REBASELINE_REASON to be set, per the guard-golden hook.
